sections.name: General Knowledge / Current Affairs of India and Goa

p1.title: Passage 1
paras: The rapid expansion of Electric Vehicles (EVs) has significantly altered the global transportation landscape. Governments worldwide have promoted EV adoption through subsidies, tax exemptions, and investments in charging infrastructure to reduce dependence on fossil fuels and lower urban pollution levels. Supporters argue that EVs represent a sustainable alternative to conventional automobiles because they produce fewer direct emissions. However, environmental analysts caution that the overall ecological benefit of EVs depends largely on the energy sources used for electricity generation. In nations where coal-fired power plants dominate energy production, EVs may indirectly contribute to substantial carbon emissions. Furthermore, the extraction of rare earth minerals and disposal of lithium-ion batteries raise serious environmental and ethical concerns. Despite these criticisms, technological advancements in battery efficiency and renewable energy integration continue to strengthen the long-term prospects of EVs. Economists also note that the EV industry has created new opportunities for innovation, employment, and industrial investment. Consequently, the debate surrounding EVs is no longer limited to transportation alone but extends to broader questions of sustainability, energy policy, and economic transition.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: Cricket in modern India has evolved from a leisurely sport into a complex social and economic institution. Its growing popularity has been fueled by mass media, corporate sponsorships, and franchise-based leagues. Financial investment has improved infrastructure and global visibility, but it has also altered priorities within the game. Player selection and retention are increasingly influenced by market value and audience appeal. Technological tools such as performance analytics and video reviews have enhanced accuracy while intensifying scrutiny. Constant evaluation places psychological pressure on players and shortens professional careers. Traditional ideals of patience, sportsmanship, and long-term development often conflict with expectations of instant success. Despite these tensions, cricket continues to function as a powerful unifying force across regions and classes. Thus, the sport reflects a delicate balance between emotional attachment and commercial ambition.

questions.q: Which of the following best captures the central argument of the passage?
opts: EVs are entirely free from environmental concerns.
EV adoption involves both significant benefits and complex challenges.
Coal-based power generation should be expanded.
questions.why: Main idea: a balanced 'benefits and challenges' option. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Assistant Professor in Livestock Production and Management), May 2026.

questions.q: The author implies that the environmental success of EVs depends primarily on:
opts: The nature of electricity production systems
questions.why: Inference: 'depends largely on the energy sources used for electricity generation'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Assistant Professor in Livestock Production and Management), May 2026.

questions.q: Why does the author mention "rare earth minerals" and "lithium-ion batteries"?
opts: To note technical limits unrelated to environment
To present environmental and ethical concerns of EV production
questions.why: Purpose question: they 'raise serious environmental and ethical concerns'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Assistant Professor in Livestock Production and Management), May 2026.

questions.q: Which of the following can be logically inferred from the passage?
opts: EVs eliminate carbon emissions in all countries.
Renewable energy integration may improve the sustainability of EVs.
questions.why: Inference: 'renewable energy integration continue[s] to strengthen the long-term prospects'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Assistant Professor in Livestock Production and Management), May 2026.

questions.q: The tone of the passage may best be described as:
questions.why: Tone: weighs supporters and critics. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Assistant Professor in Livestock Production and Management), May 2026.

questions.q: The passage mainly presents cricket as
opts: a recreational activity with mass appeal
a social institution shaped by economic forces
questions.why: Main idea: 'a complex social and economic institution'. 'Purely' is too extreme. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Assistant District Educational Inspector / Teacher), Jan 2026.

questions.q: According to the passage, commercialization has most directly influenced
questions.why: Detail: selection is 'influenced by market value and audience appeal'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Assistant District Educational Inspector / Teacher), Jan 2026.

questions.why: Vocabulary in context: the next sentence speaks of 'constant evaluation'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Assistant District Educational Inspector / Teacher), Jan 2026.

questions.q: The conflict between traditional ideals and modern expectations mainly concerns
questions.why: Detail: the seventh sentence. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Assistant District Educational Inspector / Teacher), Jan 2026.

questions.q: The author’s overall attitude toward the transformation of cricket is best described as
questions.why: Tone: 'a delicate balance'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Assistant District Educational Inspector / Teacher), Jan 2026.

questions.q: Choose the correct option: “Hardly had the meeting begun ______ the power failed.”
questions.why: 'Hardly/Scarcely … when'; 'No sooner … than'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Identify the incorrect sentence:
opts: He gave me a piece of advice.
questions.why: 'Advice' is uncountable; it has no plural. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct passive construction: “The committee will announce the results tomorrow.”
opts: The results will be announce by the committee tomorrow.
The results will announced by the committee tomorrow.
The results would be announced by the committee tomorrow.
The results will be announced by the committee tomorrow.
questions.why: Future passive: will be + past participle. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct modal: “______ I come in, sir?”
questions.why: 'May' for polite permission. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Identify the function of the underlined word: “He came yesterday.”
questions.why: 'Yesterday' tells when he came. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: 'Mission Samriddh Gaon', launched by Shivraj Singh Chouhan in 2026, began with pilot villages in which state?
questions.why: Budni (Sehore) and Khategaon (Dewas). Aug 2026.

questions.q: What is the target number of 'Lakhpati Didis' under the rural women's livelihood mission?
questions.why: Raised in 2026.

questions.q: Ahmedabad hosted, for the first time, a leg of the World Para Series in which sport (2026)?
questions.why: Hyundai World Archery Para Series. Sep 2026.

questions.q: Where was the final of the 2026 ICC Men's T20 World Cup played?
questions.why: India beat New Zealand by 96 runs.

questions.q: National Handloom Day (7 August) commemorates the launch of the:
questions.why: The 12th National Handloom Day was in 2026.

questions.q: Goa's first Chief Minister, Dayanand Bandodkar, belonged to the:
questions.why: CM from 1963 to 1973.

questions.q: Exercise 'Yudh Abhyas' is held between India and:
questions.why: An army exercise.

questions.q: India's first fully commercial Earth-observation constellation, approved by IN-SPACe in 2026, will have how many satellites?
questions.why: Allied Orbits consortium, to be operational by 2029.

questions.q: Francis Halzen, Nobel laureate in Physics 2026, is known for the IceCube Neutrino Observatory, located at the:
Silent Valley National Park is in:
questions.why: In the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve.

questions.q: Find the next number in the series: 3, 5, 9, 17, 33, ?
questions.why: Each term is double the previous one minus 1: 33 x 2 - 1 = 65.

questions.q: Find the next letter in the series: Z, X, U, Q, L, ?
questions.why: The steps back are 2, 3, 4, 5, then 6. L is the 12th letter, so the next is the 6th, F.

questions.q: If OFFICE is written as PGGJDF in a certain code, how is TALUKA written?
questions.why: Each letter moves one place forward: T-U, A-B, L-M, U-V, K-L, A-B.

questions.q: Sarpanch is to Panchayat as Mayor is to:
questions.why: A Sarpanch heads a Panchayat; a Mayor heads a Municipal Corporation.

questions.q: Looking at a portrait, Arun said, 'I have no brother or sister, but this man's father is my father's son.' Whose portrait is it?
questions.why: With no brother, 'my father's son' is Arun himself. So Arun is the father of the man in the portrait.

questions.q: A river flows from east to west. It turns left, and then turns right. In which direction is it flowing now?
questions.why: Flowing west, a left turn takes it south, and a right turn brings it back to west.

questions.q: Statement: "If the train is delayed, I will be late." Which judgment follows?
opts: If I am late, the train was delayed
The train causes all my lateness
I will be late if the train is delayed
questions.why: Only the restatement is certain; A reverses the if-then. GPSC CBRT, Mar 2025.

questions.q: April has 30 days. The ratio of rainy days to sunny days in April could NOT be
questions.why: 5 : 3 needs 8 parts; 30 is not a multiple of 8. The others split 30 exactly. GPSC CBRT, Mar 2025.
4 + 5 = 9. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2025.

questions.q: Statement: "Investing in renewable energy can reduce our carbon footprint." Argument A: Renewables are expensive to implement. Argument B: Renewables are key to reducing long-term environmental damage. Which is stronger?
questions.why: B speaks directly to the statement's goal; cost alone does not answer it. GPSC CBRT, Mar 2025.

questions.q: The first edition of the Organon (1810) was titled:
opts: Organon of the Healing Art (Organon der Heilkunst)
Organon of Rational Medicine (Organon der rationellen Heilkunde)
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. From the second edition (1819) the title became Organon der Heilkunst, Organon of the Healing Art.

questions.q: According to §7, the totality of symptoms is:
opts: the outwardly reflected image of the inner essence of the disease
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. §7: the totality must be the principal, indeed the only, thing the physician has to take note of in every case.

questions.q: In Kent's observations, amelioration first followed by aggravation suggests:
opts: a superficial, palliative remedy, or an incurable patient
a correct remedy in the right potency
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. The remedy has acted only superficially; the deeper state then reasserts itself.

questions.q: Which pair are the chief anti-sycotic remedies?
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Thuja and Medorrhinum are the leading anti-sycotics.

questions.q: Breathlessness with great rattling of mucus, worse at 3 a.m., in fat, sluggish patients with a tendency to cyanosis, suggests:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Ammonium carb: emphysema, weak heart, worse 3 a.m.

questions.q: Constant hunger with a 'better while eating' state, emaciation despite eating well, and enlarged hard glands suggest:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Iodium: hungry, hot, restless and emaciated; hyperthyroid picture.

questions.q: Restless, fidgety feet that must be kept moving all the time, with brain fag, suggest:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Zincum: incessant movement of the feet.

questions.q: Crataegus oxyacantha mother tincture is used as an organ remedy for the:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. A heart tonic in clinical organ therapeutics.

questions.q: Medorrhinum is prepared from:
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. Psorinum = scabies vesicle; Syphilinum = chancre; Tuberculinum = TB material.

questions.q: The abbreviation 'a.c.' on a prescription means:
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. Ante cibum; p.c. = after meals.

questions.q: 'Clarke's Clinical Repertory' (1904) is an example of a:
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. Rubrics are named after clinical conditions.

questions.q: In Kent's Repertory, the second chapter, after Mind, is:
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. The order follows Hahnemann's schema: Mind, Vertigo, Head...

questions.q: Damage to the cerebellum typically causes:
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. Resting tremor is Parkinsonian.

questions.q: The normal tidal volume of an adult at rest is about:
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. About 150 mL of it is anatomical dead space.

questions.q: Koilonychia (spoon-shaped nails) is a sign of:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. Leukonychia points to hypoalbuminaemia (GPSC Medical Officer, 2024).

questions.q: Negri bodies are seen in:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. In the hippocampus and Purkinje cells.

questions.q: The most common pattern in irritable bowel syndrome is (GPSC Medical Officer, 2024):
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. As keyed by GPSC.

questions.q: The most important mechanism in GERD is (GPSC Medical Officer, 2024):
opts: frequent transient lower oesophageal sphincter relaxations
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Transient LES relaxations allow reflux.

questions.q: Absence (petit mal) seizures show on EEG:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Treated with ethosuximide or valproate.

questions.q: The commonest heart defect in congenital rubella syndrome is (GPSC Medical Officer, 2024):
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Rubella triad: PDA, cataract, deafness.

questions.q: Kwashiorkor differs from marasmus chiefly by the presence of (GPSC Medical Officer, 2025):
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Oedema is the hallmark of kwashiorkor.

questions.q: Troisier's sign (enlarged left supraclavicular node) is seen in (GPSC Medical Officer, 2024):
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Virchow's node.

questions.q: The Parkland formula for fluid resuscitation in burns is:
opts: 4 mL × body weight (kg) × % burn in 24 hours, half in the first 8 hours
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Ringer's lactate is used.

questions.q: The Human Development Index does NOT include (GPSC Medical Officer, 2025):
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. IMR is part of the PQLI, not the HDI.

questions.q: 'Tache noire' is a post-mortem sign seen:
opts: on the skin of the back
in the eyes when the eyelids remain open
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Brownish-black discoloration of the exposed sclera.
